title: 'Unusual request': EC explains why it could not meet Rahul Gandhi-led opposition MPs
content: The Election Commission of India stated that no political party formally requested a meeting as protests occurred. Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, attempted to march towards the Election Commission to submit a memorandum. The Commission emphasized the need for parties to follow prescribed procedures when seeking meetings. After an unusual request from 240 MPs to meet at Parliament House Annexe, the Commission offered an alternative.

title: Melinda Gates, who helped libraries get $1 billion, shares three favourite books
content: Melinda French Gates has recently unveiled her top book picks, featuring compelling titles like Whistler, The Correspondent, and Theo of Golden. With a blend of renowned authors and fresh narratives, these selections resonate with readers. Gates stresses reading's significance and encourages her followers to join in sharing their own beloved books. Her dedication to libraries dates back to 1997, when she committed $1 billion to enhance global access to knowledge.

title: Humiliation, torn clothes and badges: Delhi women cops allege assault at protest sites
content: A senior Delhi Police officer addressed the treatment of women police personnel during ongoing protests. She highlighted incidents of misbehaviour and assault faced by these personnel while on duty. Videos circulating online show the challenges that women police officers encounter at protest sites.

title: Who is Dehati Madam Yashoda Lodhi, 12th-pass homemaker turned English teacher
content: Yashoda Lodhi, often referred to as 'English With Dehati Madam', has made a significant impact by teaching spoken English to rural homemakers and students. She embarked on this journey of learning English while caring for her ill husband. After Priyanka Chopra shared her video, her popularity soared to over four lakh Instagram followers. Yashoda's narrative highlights the power of resilience and serves to empower rural women by confronting societal expectations.

title: Smriti Mandhana replaces Harmanpreet Kaur as India captain: ‘Very special honour’
content: Smriti Mandhana has been appointed as the new captain of the Indian women's cricket team. She takes over the leadership role from Harmanpreet Kaur, who announced her resignation as captain. Mandhana has led India in several T20Is and ODIs prior to this appointment. The Board of Control for Cricket in India expressed confidence in her leadership abilities. Harmanpreet will remain part of the squad as a player during this transition.

title: Texas boy turns $500 prize into drive delivering 100,000 meals and 500,000 books
content: After winning a speech contest, Texas teen Orion Jean launched the Race to Kindness project, channeling his prize money into a heartfelt toy drive for hospital-bound children. His subsequent campaigns tackled food desert issues and promoted literacy among youth. Through his compassionate efforts, he has uplifted countless underserved communities, with an ambitious vision of achieving one million acts of kindness through ongoing community engagement.

title: Miami Beach’s historic Savoy Hotel could be demolished for 38-story tower
content: Plans have been submitted to demolish much of the historic Savoy Hotel to construct a new 38-story tower. This project will utilize Florida's Live Local Act to overcome local zoning regulations and historic preservation concerns. The developer aims to retain a small section of the Savoy's facade and lobby in a nod to history. Local officials and preservationists have expressed strong opposition due to potential loss of cultural heritage.

title: Jim Davidson confirms romance with Maria Rice-Mundy after split from Natasha
content: Jim Davidson has confirmed his romance with longtime friend Maria Rice-Mundy, weeks after calling off his sixth wedding to Natasha. The 72-year-old comedian said Maria is “too good to be true” and has “something special” about her. Davidson admitted he is still recovering from the split but said he would “just like to not be lonely” as they explore their relationship.

title: Lithuania ready to cover cost if US establishes military base
content: Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius has declared his willingness to finance the establishment of a permanent US military base in Lithuania. Since 2019, Lithuania has been hosting a rotating US battalion and is eager for a long-term military presence. Concurrently, the Lithuanian parliament is considering lifting constitutional prohibitions on nuclear weapons, a move that has drawn sharp criticism from Russia, citing heightened regional tensions.

title: Novak Djokovic’s record China Open win: How close is he to Roger Federer?
content: Novak Djokovic claimed his historic seventh China Open title when Alex de Minaur retired injured during the match, leading 7-6(3), 0-1. This victory also marks Djokovic's impressive 102nd ATP singles title, closing in on Roger Federer's record. Djokovic's unmatched performance at this event includes a perfect 34-match winning streak. While de Minaur lamented the premature conclusion, he remains hopeful for a rematch in next year's tournament.

title: Travis Kelce’s 87 Running Foundation: Why are Ed and Donna Kelce involved?
content: Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation has not posted since January 2026. They continue their charitable work through Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab. Donna Kelce met with Ignition Lab students during a Kansas City Chiefs game. Ed Kelce visited first graders at Operation Breakthrough. Travis Kelce’s foundation got its first post after January on Travis’ birthday.

title: BCCI secretary Saikia explains why VVS Laxman attended selection meeting | Exclusive
content: VVS Laxman, the head of the BCCI Centre of Excellence, took part in an important senior selection meeting intended to enhance the dialogue between national selectors and the Centre. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia specified that Laxman's aim was to ensure better communication about player fitness and availability, a crucial step as the team prepares for their imminent tour of New Zealand.

title: FIR against BJP BLA over 'false' Form-7 applications, first in Telangana
content: An FIR has been lodged against BJP Booth Level Agent S Balachander for allegedly filing false voter deletion requests. The complaint, initiated by an election official, triggered a police inquiry. Congress leaders claim these submissions aim to unjustly disenfranchise valid voters from the electoral list. In response, Telangana’s Chief Electoral Officer has ordered District Election Officers to take action against these fraudulent applications.

title: 'Dhappa': Cops tried to stop INDIA bloc march to EC; Rahul pulled a surprise
content: Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra gave the INDIA bloc protest against the Election Commission an unexpected second act after police tried to stop INDIA bloc march against Gyanesh Kumar and began detaining opposition MPs.

title: DRDO conducts maiden live jump of advanced high-altitude parachute in Ladakh
content: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) successfully executed its first live jump with the advanced high-altitude parachute system in Nyoma, from a height of 16,000 feet. This successful jump verified the parachute's effectiveness for mass drops, ensuring safety at high altitudes. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh commended this milestone as a testament to Aatmanirbhar Bharat, showcasing the synergy of India's defence entities.

title: US House moves to honour Indian Flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar; condemn 'act of terrorism'
content: The US House of Representatives has honored Captain Smit Machchhar through a formal resolution, celebrating his courageous defense of the aircraft against a treacherous act by his co-pilot that placed all lives at risk. The flight safely reached Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, ensuring the passengers' safety. This resolution also acknowledged the vital contributions of off-duty pilots and crew members during the incident.

title: Bhuvneshwar returns as India announce T20I and India A squads for New Zealand series
content: In a surprising turn of events, Bhuvneshwar Kumar has been reinstated to the Indian T20I squad, as declared by the BCCI. Shreyas Iyer will take the helm as captain, supported by wicketkeepers Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan. The India A team features rising stars like Rishabh Pant and KL Rahul, who are keen on capturing the selectors' attention.

title: Colorado family protects 650 acres of six-generation ranch after 150 years
content: Hutchinson Ranch, the oldest family-owned ranch in Colorado’s Upper Arkansas Valley, spans 700 acres along Highway 50. The Hutchinson family has maintained ownership for six generations, successfully implementing conservation agreements protecting 650 acres. These agreements prevent the land from being subdivided for development while allowing the family to continue ranching. Notable historic recognition occurred in 2003 when the ranch was identified among the top endangered properties in Colorado.

title: George Lucas turned California ranchland into nearly 5,000-acre Skywalker Ranch
content: Nestled in Marin County, Skywalker Ranch is a vast 4,700-acre creative sanctuary brought to life by filmmaker George Lucas. This enchanting retreat features a Victorian-style main house used for professional gatherings and boasts Skywalker Sound, operating since 1987. With amenities like themed guest rooms, diverse dining options, and a health club, the ranch remains a unique filmmaking destination, nearly fifty years after its inception.

title: Florida couple saves Sarasota cottage village from demolition, protecting 17 businesses
content: The anticipated transfer of the Historic Downtown Village in Sarasota to a developer has been called off. The cottages, which accommodate various local enterprises, will remain in the care of Alex and Marlene Lancaster. While business owners faced uncertainty regarding relocation and the emotional fallout of potential displacement, they now breathe a sigh of relief.

title: He bought an SUV for Rs 13.69 lakh; gets Rs 10.99 lakh refund + interest over issues
content: The Kurnool District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed the car manufacturer and its dealer to refund the ex-showroom price of a diesel car to its owner after the vehicle was found to have developed recurring diesel particulate filter (DPF) problems. The Kurnool District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission directed the car manufacturer and its dealer to pay the car owner Rs 10.99 lakh, which is the ex-showroom price of the vehicle.

title: ‘Special place in Indian cricket history’: BCCI hails captain Harmanpreet Kaur
content: Harmanpreet Kaur announced her decision to step down as captain of the Indian women's cricket team. Her tenure included leading India to their first Women's World Cup title in 2025. Kaur expressed her commitment to continue representing India as a player following her resignation. The BCCI lauded her impactful leadership and contributions to women's cricket in India. Kaur's leadership journey will be remembered for historic milestones and significant achievements.

title: Columnist sparks backlash with claim about Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen divorce
content: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen’s divorce has sparked fresh debate after columnist Liz Jones defended the NFL legend and said he should not be blamed for the split. Jones praised Lars Anderson’s biography for offering a balanced perspective. Anderson also revealed Brady walked away from football partly because the divorce changed his priorities and family life.

title: Evgeni Malkin breaks tradition after Alex Ovechkin’s NHL retirement announcement
content: Pittsburgh Penguins center Evgeni Malkin broke his longtime media routine Monday after Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin announced that the 2026-27 season will be his final NHL campaign. Malkin reflected on their shared history, rivalry and friendship while acknowledging the significance of Ovechkin’s decision. The moment added another emotional layer to one of the NHL’s defining rivalries.

title: 58-cent Goodwill sweater proved to be Vince Lombardi’s, sold for $43,020
content: In an incredible find, a couple bought a sweater for just 58 cents at a Goodwill store in North Carolina back in 2014. While viewing a documentary, they learned that it had ties to famed football coach Vince Lombardi, as a tag revealed its association with his tenure at West Point. Eventually, it fetched an astonishing $43,020 at auction after being consigned by Lombardi's colleague's widow.

title: Why children tell one parent everything but hide things from the other
content: It’s not uncommon for parents to observe that children tend to confide in one parent more than the other. This behavior can stem from a variety of factors, such as the child’s perception of how the parent might react. Key moments in a child’s life can also impact who they turn to for support. Encouraging open and understanding communication is crucial for fostering discussions between parents and children.

title: 'PCS officer’ bride vanishes with 14 tola gold, cash after marrying AAP neta; 6 booked

After marrying Amarinder Singh Mandofal, she left her matrimonial home with valuables and cash. Her family purported false information about her background, including her deceased parents. Mandofal discovered multiple instances of forgery regarding her identity documents and previous marriage.

title: Why Nobel physicist Francis Halzen built a giant ice cube to catch 'ghost particles'
content: Prof Francis Halzen has been awarded the prestigious Nobel Prize in Physics, recognizing his groundbreaking work in neutrino detection. His pioneering efforts led to the establishment of the IceCube observatory in Antarctica, dedicated to capturing elusive neutrinos generated by cosmic phenomena. In 2013, the observatory achieved a historic milestone by detecting the first extraterrestrial neutrinos, paving the way for new insights in neutrino astronomy and our understanding of the universe.

The Enforcement Directorate has pointed fingers at businessman Nitin Gohal, linking him to a 'cash-for-transfer' scheme.

title: US-Iran war, Trump tariff threat: Why India can't take its high growth for granted
content: While India’s domestic growth story stays resilient, the external sector risks continue, and with mounting impact and ripple effects. As the Department of Economic Affairs notes, global conditions have turned unfavourable again. Oil prices have spiked in September. Global bond yields have moved sharply higher and continue to climb.

title: Florida mom rides 7,000 miles across 48 states, donates $17,560 to family support home
content: A Florida woman completed a 7,000-mile motorcycle journey across 48 states in six days. She raised $17,560 for Quantum House, an organization that supported her during her daughter’s hospital stay. The ride attracted attention, allowing her to create awareness about the organization. Jess's daughter, who benefitted from Quantum House, joined her when she presented the raised funds.

title: No meeting request received: EC officials as Rahul, Priyanka refuse to leave protest site

Cong said they demanded a meeting to discuss alleged electoral irregularities and questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The police intervened and detained several opposition leaders as the protest escalated.

title: MMTC, STC may lose gold tax edge as 3% GST weighed
content: The proposal is aimed at ensuring that different channels used to import bullion face similar tax treatment and at reducing classification and valuation disputes that have resulted in lengthy litigation. The issue is likely to be discussed at the GST Council meeting on October 8. Currently, banks and certain nominated agencies are required to pay 3% GST when importing precious metals.

title: 103-year-old WWII veteran still tends same Maryland bar after 63 years
content: Irv Koch, a 103-year-old World War II veteran, has tended the bar in the basement of his Pasadena, Maryland, home since 1963. More than six decades later, the cash-only tavern still has no fixed opening hours, with Irv starting the day when his first customer arrives and closing when patrons leave or he gets tired.

content: Last year, three scientists won the Nobel Prize in physics for research on the strange behavior of subatomic particles called quantum tunneling that enabled the ultra-sensitive measurements achieved by MRI machines and laid the groundwork for better cellphones and faster computers.
